facts.content: Patient has been experiencing watery diarrhea for 3 days.
Watery bowel movements approximately every hour when awake, without blood.
facts.source_text: Watery BMs ~Q1 h when awake; no blood

facts.content: Patient has intermittent mid-lower abdominal cramps with severity of about 6 out of 10.
facts.source_text: Intermittent mid–lower abdo cramps (≈6/10) precede stools

facts.content: Patient experiences nausea and occasional vomiting after milk consumption.
Patient reports subjective fever and decreased urine frequency.
Patient's brother has a similar illness for 5 days.
facts.source_text: Brother with similar illness x5 d

facts.content: Patient denies any chronic illnesses.
Patient takes Paracetamol as needed.
Patient has no known drug allergies.
Patient's father has stage III colon cancer.
facts.source_text: FH: Father – stage III colon ca

facts.content: Patient lives with mother and sister.
Patient works as a government office worker in Central London.
Patient is a social smoker, occasionally smoking on Fridays.
Patient consumes about one beer on weekdays and binges alcohol 1-2 times per month.
Diagnosis of acute watery diarrhea with nausea and vomiting, likely due to viral gastroenteritis.
facts.source_text: Acute watery diarrhea with nausea/vomiting – likely viral gastroenteritis

facts.content: There is a risk of dehydration.
There is a positive family history of colon cancer.
facts.source_text: Positive FH colon ca (not contributing to current illness but noted)

facts.content: Patient is advised to take Oral Rehydration Solution (Dioralyte) over the counter and encourage clear fluids.
facts.source_text: Oral rehydration soln (Dioralyte) OTC; encourage clear fluids

facts.content: Patient advised to maintain a soft diet and advance as tolerated.
facts.source_text: Soft diet (soup, mash) → advance as tolerated

facts.content: Paracetamol can be taken as needed for pain or fever.
Patient should avoid dairy and alcohol until recovery.
Patient should contact GP if symptoms persist for more than 48 hours, worsen, if they are unable to keep fluids down, develop blood in stool, or a high fever.
facts.source_text: Safety-net: if symptoms persist >48 h, worsen, unable to keep fluids, develop blood in stool or high fever → contact GP for further eval/possible investigations
